assumptions: Input: Gaussian 30 fs transform-limited pulse (the real spectrum is measured, not given).
QWP1 / QWP2 achromatic; QWP2 crossed = the inverse plate; polariser crossed with the input; efficiency = energy behind / in front of the polariser.
eps = tan(alpha), alpha = angle of the first plate: eps is minor/major axis ratio. The alternative eps = (minor/major)^2 was tried in exploration and is discussed in the README.

Two beam readings for the cell: constant w = 1.45 mm (2.9 mm diameter on the mirrors, 'overall constant beam size') and a 450 um-waist Gaussian caustic in each 3 m pass. Neither is the paper's Kerr-matched mode.
Plane-wave 1-D in time (no radial model): no spatial averaging over the beam profile, so the efficiency is that of the beam centre.
BaF2: engine built-in (Li 1980 index), n2 = 2.0e-20 m2/W and Kerr anisotropy sigma = -1.2, both UNVERIFIED literature values. The paper's P/Pcr = 5e3 would imply n2 = 3.8e-20 at 31 GW.

XPW cut: 'holographic cut' is read as the [011]-type cut (engine kerrCutAxis [0,1,1], lab x = [100]); the tensor optimum is 25.5 deg from [100], i.e. 64.5 deg from [01-1]: the paper's 64.5 deg is read as measured from the in-plane <01-1> axis (UNVERIFIED reading; the paper names no axis).

XPW plates: two 600 um plates per pass, plane-wave 1-D with a constant beam radius, 1 % per mirror and 3 % per pass for the plates as one loss, no free-space diffraction, no spatial averaging over the beam. The beam radius on the plates is not given consistently (330 um waist and plates 1 m away give 840 um; '4 mm on the end mirrors' does not fit R = 1.5 m): three values are scanned and reported as a sensitivity, none is tuned to the result.

NER cell for the Kerr-matched mode: R = 1.5 m, mirror separation 2.9 m (our reading of 'about 3 m': its empty mode has 2.87 mm diameter on the mirrors, the paper's 2.9 mm), argon, peak power 31 GW (first pass), 12 passes.
